items.name: Completion One-Shot Signal — Dedup Concurrent Ingest
items.symbol: struct completion { done, wait }, DECLARE_COMPLETION, complete(), wait_for_completion()
items.counter_case: Node.js Promises already model completions exactly; a Completion class is just a Promise with its resolve exposed — the pattern is valuable but the naming and discipline is the steal, not a new data structure.

items.name: Lock-Ordering Comment Convention — Mandatory Acquisition Order Doc
items.symbol: Three-level lock ordering comment: group->mark_mutex -> mark->lock -> connector->lock
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded so lock ordering is irrelevant at runtime; the value is purely as documentation discipline to prevent async re-entrancy bugs during concurrent MCP calls.

items.name: Deferred Mark Destruction — Reaper Queue for Watcher Teardown
items.counter_case: The RCU generation-pointer snapshot from pass 3 already handles the read-after-free race; deferred destruction is complementary but redundant if VersionedEntityCache is implemented.

items.name: Intrusive Doubly-Linked List — Zero-Allocation LRU
items.symbol: struct list_head { next, prev }, list_add(), list_del(), list_entry() = container_of(), list_for_each_entry()
items.counter_case: JavaScript lacks container_of; the equivalent requires either a WeakMap<ListNode, CachedEntity> (O(1) but heap allocation) or embedding both node and payload in the same object (no extra allocation, but less reusable). The discipline is the steal, not a direct port.

items.name: Result<T,E> Discriminated Union — IS_ERR / PTR_ERR Error Encoding
items.symbol: MAX_ERRNO=4095, IS_ERR_VALUE(), ERR_PTR(), PTR_ERR(), IS_ERR(), IS_ERR_OR_NULL()
items.counter_case: TypeScript already has discriminated unions; this is a naming and enforcement convention, not a novel data structure. The value is in consistently applying it across all MCP tool handlers rather than mixing throw/return/null.

items.name: Dirty Entity Bitmap — find_next_bit O(N/64) Scan
items.counter_case: At <5000 entities a Set<string> iteration is fast enough; Uint32Array bitmap adds bit-manipulation complexity for a gain measurable only above ~10k entities.

items.name: Saturating Reference Count — Entity Lifetime Safety
items.symbol: REFCOUNT_SATURATED = INT_MIN/2, refcount_t, refcount_inc(), refcount_dec_and_test(), refcount_warn_saturate()
items.counter_case: Node.js GC handles most lifetime issues; refcounting only adds value for entities held across async await gaps, which the VersionedEntityCache from pass 3 already addresses via generation snapshots.

items.name: Workqueue Priority Tiers — HIGH/NORMAL/LOW Deferred Work
items.symbol: WQ_UNBOUND (bit 1), WQ_HIGHPRI (bit 4), NR_STD_WORKER_POOLS=2, struct work_struct { data, entry, func }
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded; setImmediate vs setTimeout(fn,0) is the only approximation available; true preemptive WQ_HIGHPRI has no equivalent in the event loop model.

items.name: mempool_t Emergency Reserve Pool
items.symbol: struct mempool { min_nr, curr_nr, elements[], alloc/free fns, wait queue }
items.violated_principle: Node.js GC is fast enough at Cortex's scale; pre-allocating entity objects eliminates GC pressure that doesn't measurably exist; adds significant initialization complexity for zero observable benefit

items.name: fsnotify_conn_mask Lockless Aggregate Event Mask
items.symbol: fsnotify_conn_mask(), READ_ONCE(conn->mask), aggregate OR of all attached mark masks
items.violated_principle: Cortex watches O(10) directories with a single watcher; the per-connector aggregate mask optimization only pays off when O(thousands) of marks share a connector — domain mismatch at scale

items.name: Undocumented Async Re-entrancy Constraints in Shared Mutable State
items.symbol: Three-level lock ordering comment block: group->mark_mutex → mark->lock → connector->lock
items.pattern: Cortex's watcher, KnowledgeManager, and entity cache share mutable state with no documented acquisition order or async re-entrancy constraints. Linux's fsnotify documents mandatory lock ordering with a comment block at the top of every file that touches shared state.
items.proposed_action: Add a CONCURRENCY.md (or section in CLAUDE.md) documenting: (1) which Cortex objects are shared between the watcher and MCP handlers; (2) which are safe to read without coordination; (3) which require the shadow-swap discipline from VersionedEntityCache. Add a lint rule that rejects any new method on KnowledgeManager/EntityCache that mutates state without a comment citing the applicable discipline.
